# Webhooks

Once you generate signature keys for your app (Developer Console → **Webhooks**
→ **Manage signature keys**), Box signs every webhook delivery. Each
`BOX-SIGNATURE-PRIMARY` / `BOX-SIGNATURE-SECONDARY` header is the base64
HMAC-SHA256, under that key, of the request body followed by the
`BOX-DELIVERY-TIMESTAMP` header (Box's
[Verify webhook signatures](https://developer.box.com/guides/webhooks/v2/signatures-v2/)
guide). `runtime.verifyWebhook` checks a delivery before you trust it:

```ts
import { runtime } from '@unofficialbox/box-open-sdk';

// `body`: the raw request body (bytes or string); `headers`: a `Headers`
// object or a plain record.
const genuine = await runtime.verifyWebhook(body, headers, {
  primaryKey,
  secondaryKey,
});
if (!genuine) {
  // reject: not from Box, altered, or stale
}
```

- **Pass the body exactly as received.** Parsed and re-serialized JSON won't
  verify.
- **Either key may be missing.** A delivery is genuine when the signature of
  any configured key matches, so you can rotate one key while the other keeps
  verifying.
- **Old or future deliveries are refused.** A delivery stamped more than ten
  minutes ago (`maxAgeSeconds`) or in the future fails, which blocks replays.
- **Header names match in any case**, and the comparison takes the same time
  wherever a signature differs.
